title: 8.6 Work

icans: I can find the work done by a variable force.
I can use Hooke’s Law to find the work done on a spring.
I can find the work to lift a chain or pump water by slicing.

vocab: force times ___________; W = ∫ F(x) dx for a variable force
F = kx, where k is the spring ___________
the SI unit of work: one _______________

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

blocks.stem: F(x) = (40 − x) N moves an object from x = 5 to x = 20 m. Find W.

notes: Hooke’s Law: F = kx; use the given force to find _______________ first.

blocks.stem: 3 N stretches a spring 0.25 m. Find the work to stretch it 1 m.

notes: Lifting: each slice’s weight times the _______________ it is lifted.

blocks.stem: A 40-ft chain weighing 3 lb/ft hangs from a bridge. How much work is done pulling it up?

notes: Pumping: weight density × volume of a slice × _______________.

blocks.stem: A cylinder, radius 2 ft and height 5 ft, is full of water. Work to pump it over the top?
6 N stretches a spring 0.5 m. Find the work to stretch it from 0 to 1 m.
A 20-ft chain weighing 2 lb/ft hangs from a roof. How much work to pull it up?

tickets.stem: F(x) = 3x² N from x = 0 to x = 2 m. Find W.
10 N stretches a spring 0.5 m. Find k.
A 10-ft chain, 4 lb/ft. Work to pull it up?
